title: Shameless Audacity
text: “It’s the same here at this circus, indeed. Filolial-samas, a friendly atmosphere simply won’t do here.”
The waiting area behind the monster dealer’s tent was a section even the Filolial-samas could approach. They absolutely never went near the back of the tent, though.
“Quite the state of high alert, isn’t it.”
“It’s an important enough time to warrant it, I say.”
Preparations for the Filo-tan Plan needed to be handled thoroughly, after all.
“However, is there not a considerable possibility that assailants will come after Iwatani-sama?”
Rabbit Guy raised a doubt about my proposed Filo-tan Plan. Given how flashy things had gotten since yesterday, it was certainly a plausible concern. But there was no problem, indeed.
“In that case, Older Sister will intercept them, indeed. She has more than enough skill, so rest assured.”
“Ohh my.”
“Well… she certainly does have the skill for it.”
“So that settles it—time for Big Sister and Naofumi-chan’s fun little date to begin!”
“The rest of us sisters will wait at Panda’s village, then.”
“Hey, big bro, can’t we go have some fun too?”
Keel was asking Father.
“Hmm. Just for a little while. I don’t even know how long I’m supposed to keep up being grumpy, and it’s nerve-wracking since the Filolials are so good at seeing through lies.”

Incidentally, Father had been practicing acting like the version of himself that couldn’t save people for a while now. Every so often his usual gentle self would pop out, but I figured he’d managed to reproduce it decently enough.
“Well, whatever… For now, as part of the reenactment, I’ll go greet the old man at the weapon shop, then stay in Lute Village helping with the reconstruction.”
“I leave it to you, indeed.”

It suddenly occurred to me—what exactly was that loop where some mysterious race ended up happening in Lute Village? What I needed to be careful of was the possibility of Itsuki receiving territorial rights from Trash or something like that. That would be troublesome, indeed. It could lead to results diverging from my predictions. Still, the Filo-tan had come to be, so surely it would be fine? Hiii…
“Well, I’m off then.”
“Safe travels, indeed. Leave the rest to me.”
“By the way, what should we do?”
“Once you’ve erased Father’s scent, you lot can just go help the monster dealer, indeed.”
“I see. Shion is tending to someone named Éclair, I believe.”
Crocodile Guy seemed to still be at the side of Éclair, whose condition wasn’t fully recovered yet. Well, from the looks of it, I figured she’d bounce back to full strength soon enough.
“So, Spear Hero-sama, what will you be doing?”
“I’m off to the castle to collect the reward money together with Yuki-chan and Kuro-chan, indeed.”

The MVP of the wave battle was Kuro-chan, indeed. Ren had just been riding on his back. Kou wanted to stay behind and help care for the villagers alongside Elephant, so he was staying to mind the fort.
“Kuro-chan seems eager to go see Ren too, it seems.”
“Yep. The Shadow Saint’s coming, right? Then Kuro’s coming too.”
“The nerve to go under those circumstances is honestly admirable. Isn’t it, Wolf?”
“Wauf.”
“Take what you can get. This is a life lesson passed down directly from Father, indeed.”
I never taught you that, Father seemed to be saying somewhere in the back of my mind, but it might as well count as teaching, indeed.
“As if you don’t already earn plenty without it…”
This Rabbit Guy sure had a lot of nagging complaints, indeed.
“Ah, right, indeed. Rabbit Guy.”
“Is that what you’re calling me now? What is it?”
“You have an important mission, indeed. A role perfectly suited to you.”
I made sure to flash a smile dripping with sarcasm, aimed squarely at Itsuki.
“Later I’ll properly level you up, maxing out your defense and speed stats until you’re nice and tough, indeed.”
“What are you planning to make me do!?”
“That’s a treat for later, indeed. Ah, and make sure you perform the act exactly as I instruct, indeed.”
“You’re clearly about to make me do something life-threatening! Somebody save me!”
“Wauf?”
“Hm… already heading out? Off to the castle, are we?”
Éclair had arrived together with Crocodile Guy.
“Indeed.”
“Then I shall accompany you as well…”
“Éclair-sama.”
“Shion, you stay behind here. Judging from the way things sounded when I heard the circumstances, my presence would only cause an uproar.”
“But…”
Éclair silenced Crocodile Guy with a glare, then smiled.

“It will be fine. It seems this isn’t a situation where I can simply sit quietly in a cell. From what you’ve told me, Kitamura-dono is quite skilled with a blade, is he not? Then there should be no problem.”
Crocodile Guy was staring at me. Was he trying to say “protect Éclair” or something? I’d already saved him from dying in prison—he ought to be grateful, indeed.
“Crocodile Guy, leave it to me, indeed.”
“I remain deeply uneasy, but understood… Éclair-sama, please refrain from anything reckless.”
“The situation hardly allows for such caution. Shion and everyone else are doing all they can, after all… I too must do what I am able to do now.”
“Hahaha… safe travels, then.”
“Off we go, then!”
“The Shadow Saint—jet-black fang and claw come rushing to his side.”
With the Siltvelt envoy and Rabbit Guy and Wolf making a racket to the very end as they saw us off, we headed toward the castle.

We passed through the castle gates and made our grand appearance at the morning audience. Ah, Itsuki was there. Was he still grumbling about wanting to declare the abolition of slavery, same as always?
“At this rate, the push toward abolishing slavery entirely will… no, the fundamental cause is…”

Same as ever, it seemed. He looked even more sour than the Itsuki I remembered. After confirming I’d arrived, Itsuki glanced around restlessly. What was that about? Looking for Father to pick a fight with, perhaps?
“Father isn’t coming, indeed. He said as much from the start.”
“I see… Motoyasu-san, what about you?”
“I came to collect what’s owed to me. Father and I are separate matters, indeed. Kuro-chan worked hard, after all.”
“……Well, I won’t deny that he was active in the fight alongside Ren-san.”

That much was an unshakeable fact, indeed. If Itsuki’s assessment turned out too low, I’d have to dish out fitting punishment to Trash. Perhaps drag out the Crimson Swine and roast her face right in front of him? No, getting carried away had its limits, indeed. That would be punishment for angering a Hero. It suddenly struck me—what kind of reaction would Trash have shown if I’d brought Tiger Girl right in front of him at that party venue where the duel took place? Well, having the Crimson Swine around would’ve just made things complicated, so probably best not to have done that, indeed. If handled poorly, Tiger Girl might have ended up assassinated just like Fleon-chan. Unfortunately, I had no interest in going along with anything involving the Crimson Swine’s poison.
“And who is this woman with you?”

“It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance. My name is Eclair Seaetto. From what I have heard, I take you to be the Bow Hero-dono. I understand there has been much history, but I hope for good relations going forward.”
Éclair offered Itsuki an oddly formal bow.
“Ah… so you’re the knight Naofumi-san mentioned. Did you really protect the demi-humans from the slave hunters?”

“Indeed. Taking advantage of my father’s death, certain men committed the outrage of slave-hunting, and I was in the midst of dispensing judgment upon them when I was captured myself. I waited in the cell for the Queen to arrive, but it seems this is not a time to remain quietly in a cell awaiting judgment, so I have come out as you see.”
“Bow Hero-dono, along with Shield Hero-dono, I wish to apologize on behalf of the Queen for dragging you both into the circumstances plaguing this country.”

Itsuki turned his face toward his subordinate Smoked Meat, apparently wanting to confirm the truth of the matter. That one wasn’t likely to say anything sensible, I figured. Just in case he tried to kick up a fuss, I leveled my spear at him in intimidation, thinking I’d skewer him if he stepped out of line—Smoked Meat glared back at me with a look of pure resentment.
